answer: Latency-anchored identity binding. Each agent must complete a fixed sequence of timed challenges tied to a shared reference clock, with progress recorded in a public nebula ledger. Cloning forces the attacker to run every duplicate through the same full sequence, costing real compute and wall-clock time per identity. An onyx threshold certificate issued only after sequence completion gates participation. The atlas index links each certificate to its accumulated cost, so mass duplication multiplies expense linearly instead of amortizing it.
